# UBSAN ignorelist -- known-benign integer sanitizer findings
# Used with -fsanitize-ignorelist= (compile-time suppression)
# Reference: https://clang.llvm.org/docs/SanitizerSpecialCaseList.html
#
# These are NOT bugs. They are correct code that -fsanitize=integer
# flags because the integer sanitizer catches well-defined but
# potentially surprising unsigned arithmetic.
#
# See also: issue #763 for vptr runtime suppression pattern

# RFC 1321 MD5 uses intentional unsigned 32-bit wrapping arithmetic
# and bit rotation via left shift -- all well-defined for unsigned types
# Fires in: IccMD5.cpp MD5Transform() lines 185-254
[unsigned-integer-overflow]
fun:*MD5Transform*

# libstdc++ 15 container internals use unsigned decrement / subtract idioms at
# loop and capacity boundaries. IntegerSanitizer reports these implementation
# details before iccDEV code has an actionable frame. Keep this scoped to
# standard-library source paths; do not add project-owned Icc*, Tools,
# IccConnect, AFL, or CFL paths here for this noise class.
src:*/include/c++/*/bits/basic_string.h
src:*/include/c++/*/bits/basic_string.tcc
src:*/include/c++/*/bits/stl_bvector.h
src:*/include/c++/*/bits/stl_uninitialized.h
src:*/include/c++/*/bits/vector.tcc
src:*/include/c++/*/ext/string_conversions.h

[unsigned-shift-base]
fun:*MD5Transform*

# Apple libc++ hashes through intentional unsigned left-shift wrapping.
src:*/include/c++/v1/__functional/hash.h
